text: The Race: which card game is this?

bank.q: Shout its name when two matching cards land on top of each other
A game for one, building down in alternating colours; Americans call it Solitaire
Bet on your hand, where a royal flush beats everything
Two partnerships bid for tricks, and one hand is laid face up as 'dummy'
Collect sets and runs, then lay them down to go out
Get as close to 21 as you can without going bust, against the dealer
Scored with pegs on a wooden board: 'fifteen two, fifteen four...'
A trick-taking game for two pairs with no bidding, the ancestor of bridge
Ask another player 'Have you got any sevens?' and hope they don't send you off to the pile
Pass cards round and don't get stuck with the unmatched queen at the end
Collect all four members of families like Mr Bun the Baker
Compare stats like speed or height to win your opponent's card
A pub game with lives: swap with your neighbour to avoid holding the lowest card
Avoid winning any heart in a trick, and above all the queen of spades
A rummy-style game from Uruguay, played with two packs and jokers, chasing sets of seven
Bet on 'player' or 'banker' in the casino game James Bond plays in 'Dr. No'
Build out from the four sevens, up and down in each suit
Lay cards face down, say what they are, and hope nobody calls you a liar
Match the suit or number of the top card; an eight lets you change the suit
Turn cards over in turn; a court card or ace makes your opponent pay up to four cards
Business at the front, party at the back
A towering 1960s 'do' piled high on the head, as worn by Amy Winehouse
Head shaved on both sides, leaving a tall strip down the middle: a punk favourite
Hair swept up and back at the front, as worn by Morrissey and Tintin
A straight cut level with the jaw, all the way round
A very short, cropped women's style made famous by Twiggy
Naturally curly hair grown out into a big round halo
Hair matted into rope-like strands, as worn by Bob Marley
Hair braided close to the scalp in neat straight lines
Very short all over, a little longer on top: the classic military trim
Looks like someone put a pudding basin on your head and cut round it
A layered, bouncy cut named after a 'Friends' character
Shaved short at the sides and back with long hair on top: the 'Peaky Blinders' look
Long hair from one side swept across to hide a bald patch
A 1990s boys' cut, parted in the middle and hanging either side of the face
Short at the sides and dead flat across the top, as on Dolph Lundgren in 'Rocky IV'
Teased and backcombed into a big rounded puff, a 1960s favourite of Dusty Springfield
A smooth knot or coil of hair pinned at the nape of the neck
Chemically set curls, a huge 1980s craze among footballers
Two ponytails, one on either side of the head
